tasks.short: Acquire, store and distribute workplace supplies.

steps.what: Inspect supplies and gather requests from workplace teams.
Reconcile stock, requests and outstanding orders in the stock workbook.
Approve quantities, substitutions and spending against the available budget.
Create and release the purchase order to the selected supplier.
Receive deliveries and check quantities, damage and substitutions.
Label accepted supplies and put them in suitable storage locations.
Distribute supplies to requesters and note quantities issued.
Update the stock workbook from receipts and issues.

tasks.design: Configure a stock register and receipt forms in the {WORKFLOW}, connected to orders in the {PROCUREMENT}. Deterministic rules propose replenishment from counts, requests and open orders; people approve spending and order release. Receipt and issue entries update stock directly, removing the separate workbook update.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical counts, purchasing records and local requests were disconnected. Connecting them cost more than the apparent clerical saving.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and purchasing approvals cover much of the process. AI coding can shorten work on connectors and replenishment rules; no model loop is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded withdrawals, delivery problems and physical handling remain. Stock rules need adjustment for seasonal demand and unusual events.
tasks.human_edge: People judge whether substitutes are suitable, recognise damaged goods and organise practical storage and distribution.

ambition.what: Weekly replenishment decisions by storage location using actual consumption and outstanding orders.

tasks.altitude: The coordinator spends less time reconciling records and more time resolving shortages and improving storage. The role gains responsibility for proposing replenishment changes; spending authority stays with the budget owner.

reach.task: Investigate differences between recorded stock and physical counts.
reach.learn: Learn stock movement controls, units of measure and cycle counting.

reach.task: Compare supply service levels across workplaces.
reach.learn: Learn demand segmentation and service-level measures.

evidence.claim: Slim4 forecasts and sets stock by item and store; office-supply suitability and savings are not established.
Structured stock movements and purchase approvals can use deterministic rules while physical handling remains human.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured customer results.

assumptions: The baseline is routine workplace consumables, with physical handling included in task effort.
The company uses the {PROCUREMENT} for orders and a local {SPREADSHEET} for stock.
The situational-input prior fits counting and exceptions; replenishment calculations become structured once movements are recorded.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot and reusable configuration, not a warehouse replacement.
Named requester records require GDPR access and retention controls. Consultation under national rules may apply if employee activity is tracked.
unknowns: Which sites, supplies and staff perform this work.
Whether existing stock features already cover the requirement.
Available interfaces, supplier catalogues and approval limits.
Accuracy of stock counts and frequency of unrecorded withdrawals.
Applicable national consultation requirements and access lead times.
research_questions: Does the existing {PROCUREMENT} support stock movements and location-level replenishment?
What minimum receipt and issue capture produces reliable stock balances?
new_work: Review shortage, substitution and delivery exceptions.
Maintain item codes, storage locations and replenishment limits.
Investigate missing movements and failed order synchronisation.
Check access rights and retention for requester records.

tasks.short: Teach staff facility procedures and verify practical understanding.

steps.what: Choose training needs from procedure changes, incidents and staff questions.
Prepare instructions, demonstrations, exercises and knowledge checks.

loop.input: Training brief and current approved procedure.
loop.output: Draft training pack with procedure references and proposed knowledge checks.
loop.check: Verify procedure version and references; procedure owner checks every operational and safety instruction.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per module; unsupported instructions are removed or returned for manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning varied procedure prose into clear explanations and realistic exercises requires language adaptation.

steps.what: Approve training instructions and practical assessment criteria.
Arrange attendance, room access and training equipment.
Demonstrate procedures, answer questions and assess practical understanding.
Record attendance, assessment results and refresher dates in the {LMS}.

tasks.design: A bounded drafting loop turns approved procedures in {DOCS} into training packs for procedure-owner approval. Configure {LMS} and {CALENDAR} for enrolment, attendance capture and refreshers, while the instructor retains demonstrations and practical assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation requires adapting site-specific instructions for different audiences. Attendance administration is separate from the physical demonstration.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can shorten preparation, and existing learning workflows can handle scheduling and records. Neither removes the need to observe safe practice.
tasks.still_hard: Hands-on competence, language needs, accessibility and questions about unusual site conditions require a skilled instructor.
tasks.human_edge: Notice confusion, adapt the explanation and judge whether someone can carry out the procedure safely.

ambition.what: Provide short site-induction sessions for evening-shift contractors.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time writing packs and chasing attendance, leaving more room for practical coaching. They retain instructional judgement; the procedure owner retains content approval.

reach.task: Coordinate induction across shifts and sites.
reach.learn: Adult learning, accessible materials and evidence of practical competence.

evidence.claim: Procedure-based drafting can assist training preparation, subject to content review; no facilities-specific case is supplied.
Learning-system configuration can administer enrolments, completion records and refresher dates.

assumptions: Current approved procedures exist and have named owners.
A learning system is available; otherwise a simple training register is needed.
Recorded completion follows instructor-entered assessment results.
Access work covers GDPR retention and permissions; employee consultation follows national rules where training records or assessment practices change.
unknowns: Which training requires authorised instructors or formal certification.
Whether contractors can access the learning system.
Languages, accessibility needs and shift coverage.
Current retention rules for attendance and assessment records.
research_questions: Which modules can use existing templates without model drafting?
Which national rules or certification schemes require practical assessment?
new_work: Review generated packs against approved procedures.
Withdraw outdated packs when procedures change.
Correct attendance exceptions and failed record transfers.
Check whether training improves observed practice.
tasks.statement: Conduct classes to teach procedures to staff.

tasks.short: Arrange lawful reuse or disposal of surplus and unclaimed property.

steps.what: Inspect property and record its identity, condition and location.
Find ownership records, asset details and previous claim correspondence.
Confirm disposal rights, resolve claims and release property from retention holds.
Choose and approve reuse, sale, donation or disposal for cleared property.
Circulate approved reuse opportunities and collect internal requests.
Agree the recipient, collection arrangements and required disposal evidence.
Supervise handover and verify property preparation and custody evidence.
Check and file handover records and required disposal certificates.
Reconcile disposal proceeds and retire relevant assets from the finance register.

tasks.design: Configure a disposal register in the {WORKFLOW}, linking ownership evidence in the {DOCS} to asset records in the {ERP}. Required clearances unlock reuse notices and collection booking; people approve the route, recipient and physical handover. Structured evidence checks prepare the asset retirement for finance approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Ownership, custody and asset records sit in separate places. Low disposal frequency makes bespoke automation difficult to justify.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, permissions and approval flows can hold the evidence together. Small deterministic connectors can prepare records without interpreting disposal rights.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed ownership, hazardous materials, data-bearing equipment and specialist waste routes need qualified judgement. Documents cannot prove that physical preparation or destruction occurred.
tasks.human_edge: People establish authority to dispose, assess condition and risk, and witness the actual handover.

ambition.what: An internal surplus-property exchange with condition records and documented custody transfers.

tasks.altitude: The facilities manager spends less time chasing records and can offer departments a reliable reuse route. Disposal authority remains subject to ownership clearance, delegated limits and finance approval.

reach.task: Maintain a complete disposal evidence trail.
reach.learn: Learn retention schedules, record identifiers and evidence completeness checks.

reach.task: Record custody transfers and reconcile property movements.
reach.learn: Learn asset identification, handover controls and discrepancy handling.

evidence.claim: Registers, evidence checklists and approval routing can be configured without a model loop.
Physical custody, ownership disputes and specialist disposal requirements retain substantial human work.
The digest provides no direct facilities-disposal case; effort and build ranges are planning estimates.

assumptions: The baseline is occasional batches of workplace furniture, equipment and unclaimed items.
Step shares average across routes; reuse requests, sale proceeds and asset retirement apply only where relevant.
The property owner can grant clearance or obtain legal advice when ownership is disputed.
Specialist teams supply preparation evidence for data-bearing or hazardous items.
GDPR applies to claimant details and personal data on equipment. National rules govern unclaimed property, disposal and any employee consultation.
Consent and access ranges cover initial permissions and any required consultation; contested cases may take longer.
unknowns: Property ownership, claim periods and retention holds.
Delegated disposal limits and required finance approvals.
Waste categories and approved collection providers.
Whether asset identifiers reliably link physical items to the {ERP}.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which existing {WORKFLOW} and {ERP} features support disposal evidence and asset retirement?
Which disposal routes require specialist certificates or witnessed preparation?
new_work: Resolve unmatched assets and incomplete ownership evidence.
Maintain disposal routes, recipient eligibility and approval limits.
Review missing certificates and failed asset updates.
Periodically check access, retention and custody records.
tasks.statement: Dispose of, or oversee the disposal of, surplus or unclaimed property.

tasks.short: Assess, negotiate, approve and administer facility leases.

steps.what: Agree space needs, location constraints and affordability with department leaders.
Request availability, floor plans and commercial offers from landlords or agents.
Visit shortlisted properties and assess suitability and operating constraints.
Read offers and draft leases to summarise costs, obligations and critical dates.

loop.input: Offer documents and draft leases, with document identifiers and page references.
loop.output: Structured rent, charges, indexation, term, break rights, notice dates and obligations with clause citations.
loop.check: Validate field types and date logic; require source passages and human confirmation of material terms.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document within a fixed page budget; unresolved fields go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Lease wording and layouts vary. Fixed templates cannot reliably locate conditional terms and cross-references.

steps.what: Compare lease costs and occupancy scenarios in a financial workbook.
Negotiate rent, flexibility, repairs and other commercial terms.
Review final clauses and confirm obligations, execution requirements and critical dates.
Approve the lease commitment and business case within delegated authority.
Execute the approved lease with the landlord.
Register the executed lease, obligations, review dates and notice deadlines.

tasks.design: A bounded extraction loop prepares cited lease comparisons from the {DOCS}; deterministic calculations produce cost scenarios. The {WORKFLOW} routes legal and budget decisions, and the {ESIGN} handles approved execution where legally suitable. The {CLM} registers confirmed terms and sends deadline alerts after verifying that the executed document matches the approved version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lease clauses vary, while costs and deadlines are copied between documents and workbooks. Integrating these records was difficult to justify for occasional transactions.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can draft cited fields for review. Existing approval and signature features, plus small calculation and document-version checks, cover the remaining administration.
tasks.still_hard: Conditional break rights, repair liabilities, uncertain service charges and local execution formalities need expert review. Physical suitability and negotiation remain substantial work.
tasks.human_edge: The manager weighs location, flexibility and operating risk, negotiates trade-offs and builds agreement with users and landlords.

ambition.what: Quarterly lease-option reviews comparing renewal, relocation and space reduction before notice deadlines.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time abstracting documents and rebuilding comparisons, and more time testing occupancy choices. The role gains responsibility for presenting earlier lease-option recommendations; legal, spending and signature rights remain with their designated roles.

reach.task: Compare occupancy scenarios and their financial consequences.
reach.learn: Learn discounted cash flow, sensitivity analysis and explicit treatment of uncertain costs.

reach.task: Plan lease-dependent fit-out and relocation milestones.
reach.learn: Learn dependency mapping, decision deadlines and contingency planning.

evidence.claim: Document extraction can draft cited lease fields, but material terms require validation and legal interpretation.
Cost scenarios, approval routing and deadline reminders can use deterministic calculations and configuration.
The digest provides no direct facilities-leasing case; proposed effort reductions and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: The baseline is leasing premises for the company's own use.
The company keeps leases in the {DOCS} and maintains a basic register in the {CLM}.
The first release covers a limited set of lease languages and document formats.
The final lease abstract is checked against the approved execution version.
Automatic registration stops if the executed document cannot be matched to the approved version.
GDPR applies to contact and signature data; the EU AI Act applies according to intended use. This scope does not score employees or allocate their work.

National rules may require consultation about workplace changes or different lease execution formalities. Related access and consultation are included as an initial allowance, not a guaranteed completion period.
unknowns: Number of leases, transaction frequency and document languages.
Whether the company leases as tenant, landlord or both.
Existing {CLM}, {WORKFLOW} and {ESIGN} capabilities and interfaces.
Delegated approval limits and legal review arrangements.
Availability and quality of occupancy and cost data.
Applicable national consultation and execution requirements.
research_questions: How accurately can cited extraction recover conditional notice provisions from representative leases?
Can the existing {CLM} manage obligations and approval-version matching without custom code?
Which cost assumptions materially change the renewal or relocation recommendation?
new_work: Validate extracted clauses, dates and cost assumptions.
Resolve document-version mismatches and missing annexes.
Maintain calculation rules, extraction fields and escalation recipients.
Check deadline alerts and record subsequent amendments.
Review permissions and retention for lease and signature records.

tasks.short: Monitor building conditions, assess hazards, coordinate corrective work, and verify that facilities remain safe.

steps.what: Review building alerts, open defects, and overdue inspections.
Walk the facility and check conditions against the inspection checklist.
Assess hazards and decide immediate restrictions and corrective priorities.
Send approved work requests to responsible teams and track acknowledgements.
Check reported corrections on site and confirm whether hazards remain.
Update defect status and compile the outstanding-actions summary.

tasks.design: A small integration combines alerts from the {OPS_SYSTEM} with defects and inspection dates in the {HELPDESK}. Configured routing and status updates produce an inspection queue and outstanding-actions summary; physical inspections and hazard decisions remain with the facilities manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Building alerts and corrective records sit in separate systems. Physical conditions still need inspection.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing queues and routing rules handle much of the administration. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building the connector.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden defects, unreliable sensors, and decisions about safe access require competent people on site.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising unsafe conditions in context and taking responsibility for immediate protective action.

ambition.what: Weekly review of recurring unresolved hazards across sites

tasks.altitude: The week contains less queue checking and chasing, with more time for inspections and recurring hazards. Formal authority to restrict access or approve corrective work does not change.

reach.task: Map building dependencies for critical services.
reach.learn: Recovery priorities, alternative locations, and acceptable service interruptions.

evidence.claim: Inspection queues, routing rules, and defect dashboards are established deterministic patterns.
Physical inspections and hazard assessment retain substantial human work.

assumptions: The company has building alerts and a shared defect register, although coverage varies.
Time shares describe a typical working cycle, not measured customer timings.
The design excludes surveillance analytics and automated access restrictions.
GDPR applies to personal data. National rules may require employee consultation if monitoring changes.
Build ranges cover one initial site and include access review and any applicable consultation.
unknowns: Which building systems expose usable alerts or exports?
Who can approve access restrictions and defect closure?
How complete are inspection schedules and responsibility records?
Which national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which alert combinations reliably identify issues needing inspection?
Can existing queue configuration replace a custom dashboard?
new_work: Review unmatched alerts and missing acknowledgements.
Maintain routing rules and inspection schedules.
Check connector failures and stale records.
tasks.statement: Monitor the facility to ensure that it remains safe, secure, and well-maintained.

tasks.short: Oversee renovations, coordinate contractors, control changes, and verify regulatory and operational readiness.

steps.what: Collect drawings, surveys, previous certificates, and proposed project scope.
Define project requirements with technical specialists and identify required permissions.
Build the programme, cost plan, dependencies, and disruption schedule.
Approve scope, funding, disruption, and conditions for starting work.
Inspect progress, coordinate contractors, and resolve site conflicts and proposed changes.
Compile progress, changes, risks, and unresolved actions into the project report.

loop.input: Current project records and dated site notes with record identifiers.
loop.output: Draft project report with cited findings, changes, risks, and unresolved actions.
loop.check: Validate record references and calculate costs deterministically; the facilities manager checks interpretation before release.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per report; missing or contradictory evidence goes to the coordinator.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template handles tables, but varied site notes need concise narrative synthesis.

steps.what: Inspect handover, review specialist certificates, and accept completion or require corrections.

tasks.design: An evidence index in the {DOCS} feeds a project template in the {PROJECT}, with deterministic cost and dependency checks. A bounded drafting loop prepares cited progress reports, while specialists define compliance requirements and people approve funding, material changes, and handover.
tasks.previous_blocker: Project documents have inconsistent names and versions, and site updates arrive as narrative notes. Requirements and construction decisions need specialist interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: Document indexing and project templates already work. AI-assisted coding reduces connector effort, and a bounded model loop can draft reports from referenced notes.
tasks.still_hard: Unforeseen building conditions, contractor disputes, regulatory interpretation, and technical acceptance remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Resolving competing needs on site and judging whether delivered work is safe, usable, and contractually acceptable.

ambition.what: Weekly renovation disruption preview for affected building users

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling evidence and reporting, and more time resolving site issues and explaining disruption. Funding, change approval, and certification rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Maintain dependencies and assess the effect of proposed scope changes.
reach.learn: Critical-path reasoning, change control, and contingency planning.

evidence.claim: Evidence indexes, project templates, and cost checks can be implemented deterministically.
Bounded report drafting can assist with narrative site notes, subject to source and human checks.

assumptions: The initial scope is one renovation project with accessible documents and consistent project identifiers.
Specialists supply applicable requirements; the model does not certify compliance.
Material scope changes return to the authorised decision-maker before commitment.
GDPR applies to personal data in project records. National rules govern building permissions and applicable employee consultation.
Build ranges include access review and applicable consultation, excluding construction and permit lead times.
unknowns: Which approvals and permissions are required for the planned works?
Who holds technical certification and contractual acceptance authority?
How consistent are drawings, document versions, and site records?
Which building-user groups must be consulted?
research_questions: Can existing project templates cover dependency and cost checks without custom scheduling code?
How accurately can report drafts preserve unresolved issues and distinguish proposals from approvals?
new_work: Review drafted reports and unsupported statements.
Maintain document versions, requirement references, and project templates.
Resolve missing evidence and conflicting site updates.
Monitor drafting quality when project terminology changes.
tasks.statement: Oversee construction and renovation projects to improve efficiency and to ensure that facilities meet environmental, health, and security standards, and comply with government regulations.

tasks.short: Coordinate equipment maintenance and repairs, authorise work, supervise contractors, and verify completion.

steps.what: Review scheduled maintenance and outstanding repair requests.
Inspect faults with technicians and agree the required work.
Prepare the work pack with asset details, access requirements, and maintenance instructions.
Authorise expenditure, downtime, and work conditions with responsible specialists.
Confirm contractor attendance, site access, and the agreed maintenance window.
Supervise work, resolve unexpected conditions, and coordinate affected building users.
Inspect completed work and confirm readiness for return to service.
Record acceptance, attach service evidence, and update the next maintenance date.

tasks.design: Configure maintenance queues and structured completion forms in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, with work-pack generation from approved records in the {DOCS}. A booking flow uses the {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}, while people authorise commitments, supervise work, and accept return to service.
tasks.previous_blocker: Asset records, instructions, and contractor scheduling are fragmented. Diagnosis and supervision depend on local conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms and templates handle repeat administration. AI-assisted coding can make the remaining document and scheduling connections cheaper.
tasks.still_hard: Specialist diagnosis, isolation procedures, contractor quality, and unexpected faults remain demanding.
tasks.human_edge: Coordinating competent specialists and recognising when actual conditions invalidate the planned work.

ambition.what: Weekly repair-versus-replacement review for repeatedly failing assets

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into preparing packs and chasing bookings. The manager gains earlier evidence for replacement proposals; spending and technical approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Set spare-parts replenishment priorities for critical equipment.
reach.learn: Lead times, stock accuracy, and the cost of equipment downtime.

evidence.claim: Maintenance schedules, work packs, bookings, and completion records can use deterministic workflows.
Repair supervision and return-to-service acceptance require contextual technical judgement.

assumptions: The {OPS_SYSTEM} represents an existing maintenance records system.
Approved instructions and asset identifiers are available for work-pack generation.
Structured completion forms can capture key service fields without model extraction.
The manager escalates technical changes beyond delegated competence or spending authority.
GDPR applies to contractor and employee data. National rules determine any consultation requirements.
Build ranges cover a pilot equipment group, access review, and applicable consultation.
unknowns: How reliable are asset histories and maintenance intervals?
Who approves permits, technical isolation, and return to service?
Can contractors submit structured completion evidence?
Which booking and purchasing commitments require additional approval?
research_questions: Which repeated work-pack fields can be populated from existing records?
Which equipment group offers the clearest pilot without changing technical procedures?
new_work: Maintain approved work-pack templates and asset references.
Review booking exceptions and incomplete service evidence.
Check that schedule updates follow accepted work and approved maintenance intervals.
tasks.statement: Oversee the maintenance and repair of machinery, equipment, and electrical and mechanical systems.

tasks.short: Help design facility layouts, space changes and installations.

steps.what: Inspect spaces and discuss operational needs with occupants.
Combine occupant requirements, existing drawings and installation constraints into a design brief.

loop.input: Occupant requirements, site observations and installation records.
loop.output: Draft design brief with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source references; facilities manager confirms constraints before adoption.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per brief; unresolved or conflicting requirements return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requirements arrive as varied prose and annotated documents; templates alone cannot interpret them.

steps.what: Review layouts in {OTHER} building-design software with architects and engineers.
Compare capacity, costs, disruption and delivery dates across layout options.
Check technical feasibility and record conditions for the preferred option.
Approve scope, funding and acceptable operational disruption.

tasks.design: Use a brief template in {DOCS}, with a bounded extraction loop that links requirements to their sources. A deterministic comparison tool combines agreed quantities, estimates and schedules from {OTHER} building-design software and {PROJECT}; technical acceptance and funding approval remain separate human decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drawings, occupant requests and installation records have different formats. Physical constraints and uncertain estimates prevent reliable automatic design decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding can shorten implementation of document importers and comparison tools. Bounded extraction can reduce brief preparation, without solving architectural judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden services, outdated drawings, specialist engineering and disagreements about space still require investigation and negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: Connect how people actually use a building with technical constraints, accessibility and disruption tolerances.

ambition.what: Compare phased refurbishment options at each design milestone.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling briefs and comparisons, with more time on site and in design discussions. They can recommend phasing earlier; technical and funding authority does not change.

reach.learn: Dependency mapping, estimate uncertainty and change control.

evidence.claim: Templates, document extraction and deterministic option comparisons can reduce preparation work; this is not a documented facilities case.
Site investigation, technical acceptance and stakeholder trade-offs require accountable human judgement.

assumptions: The company uses external architects or engineers for specialist design.
The first version compares supplied options rather than generating construction-ready drawings.
Build ranges cover one site and one drawing exchange format.
Access work includes drawing permissions and screening personal data under GDPR; workplace consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: Whether existing drawings match the building.
Available export formats and access rights for building-design software.
Who holds technical acceptance and funding authority.
Whether the proposed workplace changes require employee consultation.
research_questions: Which drawing formats preserve room areas and installation identifiers reliably?
Which national rules govern design sign-off, accessibility and workplace consultation?
new_work: Check extracted requirements and source references.
Maintain comparison formulas and estimate assumptions.
Resolve conflicting drawing versions and missing constraints.
tasks.statement: Participate in architectural and engineering planning and design, including space and installation management.

tasks.short: Prepare facilities budgets, assess spending options, obtain approval, and monitor commitments and variances.

steps.what: Collect actual spending, open commitments, contract renewals, and planned equipment purchases.
Reconcile cost categories, commitments, and invoice timing in the budget workbook.
Agree demand, maintenance, pricing, and contingency assumptions with operational stakeholders.
Calculate budget scenarios and prepare the proposed facilities budget.
Negotiate priorities and trade-offs with the budget owner and finance team.
Approve the budget and release spending limits.
Compare actuals and commitments against budget and identify required corrective decisions.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration combines actuals from the {ERP}, commitments from the {PROCUREMENT}, and renewal dates from the {CLM}. Deterministic reconciliation and scenario calculations feed a {BI} dashboard, with budget approval configured in the {ERP} and trade-offs decided by people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costs, commitments, and renewal dates use different identifiers and reporting periods. The workbook compensates for those gaps.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable mappings and scheduled extracts make the calculations repeatable. AI-assisted coding can shorten the work needed to build and maintain those connections.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain demand, emergency repairs, poor commitment data, and contested funding priorities remain.
tasks.human_edge: Balancing safety, service quality, and financial constraints when several defensible spending choices compete.

ambition.what: Weekly review of forecast facilities spending overruns

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time collecting figures and rebuilding scenarios, and more time preparing corrective options. Budget owners retain approval rights; the manager gains timely evidence rather than new spending authority.

reach.task: Compare lifecycle costs of repair, replacement, and service-contract options.
reach.learn: Cost-driver analysis, uncertainty ranges, and whole-life costing.

evidence.claim: Budget reconciliation, scenario calculation, and variance reporting are deterministic when inputs and mappings are defined.
Funding priorities and service trade-offs remain human decisions.

assumptions: Financial systems hold actuals and purchase commitments; a workbook currently connects them to facilities planning.
The initial build covers facilities cost centres and uses approved accounting definitions.
No model loop is needed for structured budget calculations.
GDPR applies if source records contain personal data. National rules determine whether any employee consultation is required.
Build ranges include finance access approval, reconciliation testing, rollout, and applicable consultation.
unknowns: How are actuals, accruals, and open commitments currently reconciled?
Are contract renewal dates and indexation terms recorded structurally?
Who approves budgets, transfers, and emergency expenditure?
Which exports or interfaces are available?
research_questions: Can existing financial reporting configuration replace part of the proposed integration?
Which commitment and timing checks best prevent double counting?
new_work: Resolve unmapped costs and reconciliation exceptions.
Maintain cost mappings, scenario assumptions, and variance thresholds.
Check feed completeness and investigate material forecast changes.
tasks.statement: Plan, administer, and control budgets for contracts, equipment, and supplies.

tasks.short: Prepare operational reports and check facilities schedules for accuracy and efficiency.

steps.what: Export facilities-management records from {OTHER} and purchase costs from the {ERP}.
Reconcile identifiers, reporting periods and missing entries in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Calculate service measures and assemble the operational report.
Investigate material variances and approve report explanations.
Check schedule conflicts and approve revised maintenance dates with affected teams.
Send the approved report and schedule to internal service owners.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on {DATA_PLATFORM} reads {OTHER} facilities-management records and {ERP} costs, validates identifiers and generates a report in {BI}. Deterministic checks flag schedule conflicts and data exceptions; {WORKFLOW} routes report explanations and schedule changes for approval before sending notifications through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent asset identifiers and reporting periods force manual reconciliation. Reports and schedules are maintained in separate tools.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable exports, rule checks and report templates already support this approach. AI coding can reduce the cost of building and maintaining the connecting code.
tasks.still_hard: Missing service records, disputed supplier performance and operationally sensitive maintenance windows require investigation and agreement.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a reporting error from a real service failure and choose a corrective action that occupants can tolerate.

ambition.what: Review overdue critical maintenance each working day.

tasks.altitude: The manager receives exceptions and traceable figures instead of assembling the reporting pack. They can intervene sooner within existing maintenance authority; spending and shutdown approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Analyse recurring maintenance delays and cost drivers.
reach.learn: Data lineage, denominator choice and root-cause analysis.

evidence.claim: Structured exports, reconciliation rules and report templates support deterministic facilities reporting without a model loop.
Rule checks can identify schedule overlaps, but operational disruption decisions still require local judgement.

assumptions: Facilities records contain stable work-order or asset identifiers.
The first version connects one facilities-management system and one finance export.
Schedule checks propose changes rather than controlling building equipment.
Access work includes GDPR minimisation and retention; staff-level monitoring changes require assessment under national rules.
unknowns: Export availability, refresh frequency and permissions.

Definitions of critical maintenance and report approval thresholds.
Whether source logs contain personal data or reveal individual staff performance.

Maintain service metric definitions and conflict rules.
Monitor failed imports and report freshness.
Review material variances and approve schedule changes.
tasks.statement: Prepare and review operational reports and schedules to ensure accuracy and efficiency.

tasks.short: Set departmental service goals, priorities and deadlines.

steps.what: Review service performance, commitments and upcoming building needs.
Estimate team capacity and dependencies against proposed work.
Draft measurable service goals and proposed deadlines.
Agree priorities and realistic deadlines with team leads and internal customers.
Approve goals and resolve commitments beyond departmental authority.
Record goals, owners, milestones and review dates in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configure {BI} and {PROJECT} to assemble a planning baseline and publish approved milestones. A small deterministic tool calculates capacity scenarios and fills a goal template in {DOCS}; the manager chooses objectives and negotiates commitments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Performance figures, resource estimates and commitments sit in separate places. Turning them into credible priorities remains a management decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and project configuration can handle much of the coordination. AI coding makes a small capacity calculator cheaper to build and adapt.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent failures, supplier uncertainty and competing customer needs can invalidate a mathematically feasible plan.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which service compromises are acceptable and secure commitments from people with competing priorities.

ambition.what: Rebalance the maintenance backlog against capacity each fortnight.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time collecting figures and entering milestones. Within the approved budget, they can propose more frequent priority changes; approval rights remain as delegated today.

reach.task: Evaluate whether service targets improve building reliability.
reach.learn: Metric design, baseline comparison and unintended incentives.

evidence.claim: Reporting configuration and capacity arithmetic can support departmental planning without a model loop.
Selecting goals and negotiating deadlines depend on local priorities and management judgement.

assumptions: Goals concern departmental service outcomes rather than automated individual appraisal.
Resource estimates are available at team level.
The first version uses existing reporting and project permissions.
Access work includes GDPR data minimisation and consultation screening under national rules if work allocation or monitoring changes.
unknowns: Which service measures are reliable enough for planning.
How much authority the manager has to change priorities.
Whether the existing reporting and project systems can share identifiers.
Whether employee-level data or monitoring would enter the proposed scope.
research_questions: Can existing configuration produce the baseline without custom integration?
Which capacity assumptions best predict missed facilities deadlines?
new_work: Maintain capacity assumptions and service metric definitions.
Investigate stale or incomplete planning data.
Record why priorities changed and check the resulting service outcomes.
tasks.statement: Set goals and deadlines for the department.

role_batches.altitude: Facilities management remains substantially physical and relational. The week shifts from assembling records and chasing updates toward inspections, contractor coordination, and earlier maintenance and spending decisions; formal approval rights remain unchanged.
reach: Business continuity planning through critical building-service dependencies.
Project management through dependencies, disruption planning, and change control.
Inventory coordination through critical spares and replenishment priorities.
Management analysis through lifecycle costs and facilities spending scenarios.
skills_to_grow: Source checking for drafted project reports.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a weekly facilities resilience review that connects recurring hazards, failing assets, renovation disruption, and forecast spending to concrete decisions by the responsible owners.

role_batches.altitude: The facilities manager spends less time preparing packs, reconciling records and administering training. More of the week goes to site investigation, stakeholder agreement and earlier service intervention; professional, budget and safety decision rights remain explicitly assigned.
reach: Project management specialist: prepare phased installations using dependencies and change control.
Management analyst: investigate service reliability and maintenance cost drivers.
Administrative services manager: coordinate practical induction across sites and shifts.
skills_to_grow: Define service measures and understand their limitations.
Check data lineage, exceptions and generated source references.
Compare capacity, cost and disruption scenarios.
Facilitate workplace trade-offs and practical training.
Specify access, retention and consultation requirements.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a regular building-service review that connects critical maintenance, space changes, installation plans and staff readiness, with traceable evidence and clear approval routes.

role_batches.altitude: The facilities manager's week shifts from chasing stock, disposal evidence and lease paperwork towards workplace reliability and resource choices. The role gains stronger recommendation rights through better evidence; delegated spending, legal clearance and signature authority do not automatically expand.
reach: Shipping, receiving, and inventory clerks: stock accuracy and custody controls.
Management analysts: occupancy costs and scenario comparisons.
Project management specialists: lease, fit-out and relocation dependencies.
Administrative services managers: workplace service planning.
skills_to_grow: Designing practical stock and custody controls.
Checking cited document extraction against source clauses.
Managing exceptions, permissions and record retention.
Turning operational evidence into clear spending and space recommendations.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a quarterly workplace resource review that combines supply demand, reusable property and lease options into specific proposals for departmental and finance decisions.

summary.basis: 100 baseline hours; equal weight per loaded task; step shares normalized within each task
